rationale: Z24 (pass 24), from the firing half of the pass-24 GAP. `reflection-builtin-probe.mts` counted 989 `@hasDecl`/`@field` call sites on the parse tree across the whole zig corpus (8 shards, 3,848/3,848 files, 0 parse traps), of which 206 name a declaration as a string; `reflection-firing.mts` drove production `parseFile` over all 70 files carrying such a site and found 0 edges attributed to a reflection reason code. So the construct is present and was unread. This fixture pins the one construct a `uses` edge IS for (`@field(S, "x")` reads `S.x`) and pins, as FORBIDS, the two things a permissive implementation would get wrong. The `@hasDecl` forbid is the substantive one: an existence test whose surrounding code handles both answers, so an edge would assert a dependency the source deliberately does not take. The non-identifier forbid is second: `@field(anyerror, "Expected closing ]")` is a legal read of an error-set member, and publishing that text as a bare target is what produced junk targets once already (Z18); three corpus sites are exactly this shape and all three resolve to nothing published. Two rows pin that the emitted edge discloses its own resolvability rather than asserting a target it cannot bind — `containerMayBeAnExpression -> default` is the corpus's one application-code `@field` site (ghostty/src/input/Binding.zig:1324), where `default` has four published symbols in the file and picking one would be a guess.

expectSymbols.note: a container_field of Point, so `uses readByName -> x` resolves at both ends inside the file

expectSymbols.name: one

forbidSymbols.note: an error-set member is not a declaration this file publishes, and must never be minted as one

expectRelationships.note: the plain read. 0.75 not 1.0: the analyzer knows the member NAME and not that the declaration the graph binds `x` to is Point's own member
the same edge must be countable as a heuristic, which is what the contract requires of anything under 0.8
an ASSIGNMENT through the reflected field still names the member the function reaches
the read on the right-hand side — two edges from one source, and NOT collapsed into one
a function-valued member read by name. targetKind is the member's kind, so a consumer does not read this as a call to a function

the container is a field expression, which must not suppress the edge. Nothing publishes `default` here, and in the one application-code corpus site four symbols share it — so the edge is emitted and labelled file-external rather than attributed to a declaration by a rule nobody chose
`Type.Int` is a real read through `@typeInfo`; the name is identifier-shaped so the edge is emitted, and no per-file rule can bind it

forbidRelationships.note: THE substantive forbid. `@hasDecl(Point, "x")` is an EXISTENCE TEST and the body handles both answers, so naming `x` would assert a dependency the source deliberately does not take. Measured: 184 of the 206 named sites in the corpus are `@hasDecl`, and 128 of those name a declaration this corpus publishes nowhere — a permissive reading would have produced 128 edges the graph cannot walk to
the same existence test must not become a references edge either — that type has the same 'asserts a dependency' meaning
the member name given by a COMPTIME VALUE names nothing statically. This is the majority corpus shape — 757 of the 779 `@field` sites

a non-identifier-shaped string is an error-set member, not a member this file declares. Publishing it as a bare target is the Z18 junk-target defect; all three corpus sites of this shape resolve to nothing published

the reason code must be the reflection one. A dot-access spelling does not occur here, so an implementation that reused the zig_field_access code would be indistinguishable to a consumer reading only the label — which is the whole reason a second code exists
